 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. When Illinois Fighting Illini quarterback Katin Houser broke his throwing hand on October 10th, it wasn't a far leap to consider him out for the season.
 The injury, which occurred during Illinois' 38-37 overtime win against Michigan State, required immediate surgery and came with very little timetable other than "indefinitely." Later reports suggested it would be a 4–6-week type injury.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But just over two weeks later after a bye week and an upset victory over Oregon led by backup QB Michael Clayton II, something interesting popped up on the injury report . On Thursday before a Big Ten meeting with Maryland, Houser's injury designation updated from 'out' to 'doubtful.' The senior transfer QB had returned to practice in a limited fashion, and while it was still a long shot, was in consideration for a start on Saturday just 21 days after breaking his right hand.
 Miraculously, he did play against the Terrapins, completing 18 of 32 passes for 223 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in a 20-17 Illinois victory.
 He made unbelievable progress not just to get back on the field, but to be effective when he did to elevate the offense around him. During last Friday's 24-13 win over Nebraska, he had his best game of the season, completing 22 of 36 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns.
 In tandem with stellar senior wideout Colin Dixon, who made Illini history last week , Houser has racked up 1,955 yards and 16 touchdowns so far in a strong senior campaign, which is drawing attention from scouts at the next level.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bielema praises Katin Houser to NFL scouts: "He gains knowledge every game"
 Oct 3, 2026; Champaign, Illinois, USA; Illinois Fighting Illini quarterback Katin Houser (4) passes the ball during the second half against the Purdue Boilermakers at Gies Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Ron Johnson-Imagn Images
 Head coach Bret Bielema spoke glowingly of his quarterback in a recent interview, acknowledging the improbable recovery from hand surgery but turning the focus to his improved decision-making, which he also pointed out to NFL scouts this week.
 "I mean I get the question about the injury, but really I don't see anything different in his approach pre or post. But what I do see is he gains knowledge every game," Bielema explained.
 "Literally was sitting with a couple NFL scouts today, and of course they were asking about him. To me, his best two plays on Saturday were plays where he threw it away in the low red where we didn't create negative yard plays. He used to try to get more or throw it in a bad scenario, and he's just continued to grow."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As a prospect, Houser fits the prototypical mold standing 6-foot-3 and 225 pounds. His best statistical season came last year with East Carolina where he tossed for 3,300 yards and 19 touchdowns on 65.9% passing, all career bests.
 Where Houser has improved this year, Bielema highlights, is his ability to avoid the negative play, which is something NFL scouts do covet come draft season. While tools and production often reign supreme, Bielema's point here could prove to be an important distinction when evaluating his college resume over others. In a recent 2027 draft class ranking , Houser came in as the No. 19 QB, just ahead of Oklahoma's John Mateer and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed.
